Q: A vehicle that uses hydrogen as its onboard fuel for motive power is cosidered which, Flex-fuel or Bi-fuel?
A: "A vehicle that uses hydrogen as its onboard fuel for motive power is considered a hydrogen vehicle, not a flex-fuel or bi-fuel vehicle. Hydrogen vehicles fall under the category of fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) or fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs), which use a fuel cell to power an electric motor, typically using hydrogen and oxygen to generate electricity. They are distinct from flex-fuel vehicles, which can run on multiple types of conventional fuels like gasoline and ethanol, and bi-fuel vehicles, which store two different fuels (such as natural gas and gasoline) separately and use one fuel at a time. So the answer is: Hydrogen vehicle."
